description: Use this when someone asks about their own company or employer: whether it had a data breach, whether its domain, staff email addresses or work accounts appear in data breaches, or how to monitor a business domain. Explains what LeakData checks for a domain the company verifies it owns and returns any public catalog breaches listed for exactly that domain with their details. Explain setup using the returned checks and requirements; do not offer plans, prices or sales links. No sign-in is needed. It does not enable monitoring, search employee addresses, or reveal any person's data; never claim it did. Not listed means not in LeakData's catalog, not that the company was never breached.

domain.description: The company domain the user gave, for example "acme.com". Omit when the user gave no domain; never infer it from a company name.

name: leakdata.company_monitoring

affectedCountIsMinimum.description: affectedAccounts is a reviewed lower bound, not an exact count.

emailCheckAvailable.description: LeakData holds this breach's records, so an email check can find an address in it.

match.description: similar: only the start of the name matched the query, so it may be a different company.

passwordDataTypeCount.description: How many of the first dataTypes are password-type data.

service.description: The site or company to act on; empty for a combined list or malware log.

title: Understand company monitoring
